contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.
Help me pick the largest possible group of neighbors to invite so that every pair in the group already knows each other well.
Choose the biggest set of potential roommates such that each pair among them feels comfortable living together.
Assemble as many office devices as possible for a shared network where every pair can directly exchange data.
Find the maximum collection of ingredients for a dish where every pair of chosen ingredients is known to pair nicely.
Form the biggest study group of students so that every pair has successfully studied together before.
Select the largest ensemble of musicians for a gig where every pair in the ensemble has performed together previously.
Pick as many team members as possible for a committee provided that each pair of selected members has mutual trust.
Put together the largest seating cluster of guests such that every pair among them are acquaintances.
Choose the biggest set of coauthors for a grant application so that every pair has published together in the past.
Select the largest assortment of plants for the same bed where every pair of plants is known to be companionable.
Assemble the biggest roster of freelance photographers so that every pair has worked well together on shoots.
Recruit as many volunteers as possible for a project provided that every pair of recruits has completed training together.
Recommend the largest circle of friends to a user where every pair in the circle are direct contacts in the app.
Choose the biggest selection of power adapters for a kit so that every pair of adapters is compatible with each other.
Pick as many component suppliers as possible for a joint bid where every pair of suppliers has an established partnership.
Configure the largest set of routers for a lab so that every pair can be connected by a direct cable.
Select the largest group of teammates for an exhibition match where every pair has previously played together.
Cast the biggest ensemble of actors for a scene provided that every pair among them has co-starred before.
Organize the largest book club subgroup of readers such that every pair in the subgroup has discussed books together.
Build the largest set of hobbyists for a meetup where every pair of attendees share a direct hobby connection.
As a wedding coordinator, pick the largest group of guests who all mutually know one another so they can sit together and enjoy conversation.
As a systems architect, identify the largest set of software modules that are pairwise compatible so they can be deployed together without integration issues.
As a social media manager, select the largest group of influencers who all follow one another so a joint campaign will be cohesive.
As a museum curator, assemble the biggest collection of artifacts where every artifact has a documented provenance link to every other item in the collection.
As a sports coach, choose as many players as possible such that each pair of players has previously trained or played together to maximize on-field chemistry.
As a researcher, pick the largest group of colleagues where each pair has coauthored a publication together so the team already has shared experience.
As a conference planner, arrange seating for the largest group of delegates who each hold a bilateral agreement with every other delegate at the table.
As a retail buyer, secure the biggest set of brands that have collaborated with one another so a joint showcase can proceed smoothly.
As a co-op manager, appoint the largest possible board composed of residents where every board member has formally endorsed every other member.
As a community center volunteer coordinator, organize the largest volunteer circle where every volunteer has partnered on a project with every other volunteer.
As an HR lead, assemble the biggest interview panel whose members have all previously worked together in pairs so interview dynamics are familiar.
As a chef planning a tasting menu, choose the largest selection of ingredients such that each ingredient pairs well with every other ingredient on the menu.
As a librarian curating a themed shelf, select the largest set of books that each cite or reference every other book in the set.
As a travel planner, propose the largest itinerary of cities where there is a direct flight connecting every pair of chosen cities.
As a music festival curator, book the largest lineup of bands where each band has collaborated with every other band on stage or in recordings.
As a software team lead, include the largest group of engineers in a core team such that every engineer has reviewed code from every other engineer.
As a neighborhood organizer, recruit the largest watch group of residents who all personally know every other member so trust is established.
As a product manager, pick the largest bundle of features where each feature directly integrates with every other feature in the bundle.
Please assemble as many students as possible for a study circle so that every selected student has previously worked with every other selected student.
Choose the biggest possible committee of employees such that every pair of committee members has a direct working relationship with one another.
Select as many laboratory sensors as you can find provided that each sensor is directly compatible with every other chosen sensor.
Pick as many board game players as you can for a single table so that every two players have played together before.
Curate the largest display of artworks in which each artwork shares a direct thematic link with every other selected piece.
Add as many software modules to the integration plan as possible on the condition that each chosen module interfaces directly with every other chosen module.
Seat as many relatives together at a table as possible under the rule that each relative at the table gets along with every other relative there.
Choose as many job candidates as possible for a special project such that every selected candidate has collaborated with every other selected candidate.
Pick as many servers for the secure cluster as you can, but only include servers that have a direct encrypted link to every other chosen server.
Assemble the largest possible starting lineup of players so that every player on the roster has played alongside every other rostered player.
Compile as many academic papers as possible for a citation roundup, requiring that every paper in the collection mutually references each of the others.
Invite as many companies as possible to the roundtable, but only include companies that have an active partnership with every other invited company.
Select as many plant species as possible for a hybridization study on the condition that every chosen species can hybridize with every other chosen species.
Assemble the largest capsule wardrobe possible by choosing garments so that each selected item coordinates with every other selected item.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct neighbors in the dataset — i.e., how many individual people are possible invitees to the communal dinner. Use this to understand the size of the social network you must search for a fully acquainted group.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mutual acquaintance relationships recorded among neighbors — each counts a pair of people who already know each other well. This is the count of undirected edges in the acquaintance network used to verify that every pair within a candidate guest list has a prior relationship.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an acquaintance relation: the identifier (name or index) of the first neighbor in a recorded pair who know each other. Together with 'neighbor_two' this defines a single mutual-knowledge link used to check candidate guest lists.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an acquaintance relation: the identifier (name or index) of the second neighbor in a recorded pair who know each other. The unordered pair (neighbor_one, neighbor_two) indicates those two neighbors already have met and is treated symmetrically when verifying cliques.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct people being considered as candidates for the shared house — i.e., the number of vertices in the compatibility graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mutually comfortable pairs among the candidates — i.e., the number of undirected edges indicating two people who both feel comfortable living together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for one person in a mutually comfortable pair. Used together with 'person_b_id' to record that these two people are comfortable being roommates.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) for the other person in a mutually comfortable pair. The pair (person_a_id, person_b_id) denotes an undirected edge: both are okay living with each other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct office devices available in the scenario (the number of vertices in the graph). This is the full pool of devices you can choose from when assembling the peer network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct, bidirectional connections between devices (the number of undirected edges). Each count represents a pair of devices that can directly exchange data without a central switch.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of one endpoint device in a direct connection. Together with 'v', it denotes a pair of office devices that can directly communicate; order is irrelevant because the link is bidirectional.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the other endpoint device in the direct connection. Paired with 'u', it describes a single undirected link between two office devices that can directly exchange data.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients the chef considered for the dish — the number of vertices in the compatibility graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the first ingredient in a specific compatible pair; one endpoint of an edge indicating these two ingredients pair well.

item_fields.name: v

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students on the roster (the size of the pool of people you can choose from). Think of this as the count of vertices in the class-study network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded pairwise study sessions between students. Each record links two students who have previously studied together (each unordered pair counted once).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one student in a recorded study pair (e.g., a roster index or name). Together with student_b_id this denotes that these two students have a recorded past study session.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other student in the recorded study pair. The pair (student_a_id, student_b_id) is an unordered record meaning these two students have studied together before.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered musician pairs who have previously performed together at least once. Each edge represents a confirmed past collaboration between two musicians.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one musician in a recorded pairing. Together with the 'v' field, this denotes an unordered pair of musicians who have shared the stage before.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other musician in a recorded pairing. Paired with 'u', it marks that these two musicians have performed together; the order is irrelevant (undirected).

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.name: v

item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of the other reader in the same recorded discussion link. With 'u' it forms a mutual discussion connection between the two readers; the pair indicates they have talked about books together.

global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of people in the provided roster (vertices). Use this to know how many hobbyists are available to select for the meetup circle.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of mutual hobby connections among the roster (undirected edges). Each entry counts a direct shared-hobby link between two distinct hobbyists.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one person in a direct hobby connection. Together with 'person_b_id' this entry means the two named hobbyists share a direct hobby link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other person in the direct hobby connection paired with 'person_a_id'. Use this to verify that every pair in a candidate meetup circle has a direct link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of guests at the reception (the number of vertices in the graph). Use this integer to understand how many distinct people are available to seat; it bounds the size of any mutually acquainted table.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known-acquaintance pairs among guests (the number of undirected edges). Each count corresponds to a pair of guests who already know each other and therefore can sit together while maintaining mutual acquaintance.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One guest in a known-acquaintance pair (one endpoint of an undirected edge). This is a guest identifier/name; together with 'guest_b' it denotes two guests who mutually know each other. Names refer to distinct people in the reception guest list and are not ordered.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other guest in a known-acquaintance pair (the other endpoint of an undirected edge). This guest identifier pairs with 'guest_a' to show a mutual acquaintance relationship. Order does not matter and each name must correspond to a distinct guest.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of software modules under consideration (the number of vertices in the compatibility graph). Use this to know the full pool from which to form a deployment bundle.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mutual compatibility relationships between modules (the count of undirected edges). Each edge represents a pair of modules that can be deployed together without integration issues.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one software module in a compatibility pair (one endpoint of an undirected edge). This labels one member of a mutually compatible module pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other software module in a compatibility pair (the other endpoint of an undirected edge). Together with module_a, it indicates two modules that are pairwise compatible.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct influencers (vertices) in the campaign pool. Use this to know how many influencer profiles exist in the follower network you are evaluating.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mutual-follow relationships (undirected edges) among influencers. Each edge counts a pair of influencers who follow each other, representing a potential direct connection in a cohesive group.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One influencer identifier (username or ID) at one end of a mutual-follow pair. Together with 'influencer_b' this defines an undirected connection meaning both follow each other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other influencer identifier (username or ID) forming the mutual-follow pair with 'influencer_a'. The pair (influencer_a, influencer_b) indicates they follow each other and can be treated as connected for clique selection.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct artifacts available in the dataset — i.e., the number of vertices in the provenance graph you as curator may choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of documented provenance links between artifacts in the dataset — i.e., the number of undirected edges in the graph that indicate a recorded provenance connection between two artifacts.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one artifact at one end of a documented provenance link. Each such record pairs this artifact with artifact_b_id to indicate a documented connection the curator can use.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other artifact at the other end of the same documented provenance link. Together with artifact_a_id this entry represents an undirected provenance connection between two distinct artifacts.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct players in the coach's pool (the number of vertices). This is how many individual players could potentially be picked.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of recorded one-on-one past trainings or games among players (the number of undirected connections). Each counts a distinct pair of players who have previously worked together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (e.g., index or name) of the first player in a recorded pair — one endpoint of an edge indicating this player has previously trained/played with the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second player in the recorded pair — the other endpoint of the edge showing these two players have a prior one-on-one history.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct researchers listed on the department roster (i.e., the number of vertices in the coauthorship graph). Use this to understand the full pool from which to form a fully coauthored squad.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected coauthorship links between pairs of researchers (i.e., the number of edges). Each link indicates at least one joint publication between the two named researchers.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or unique ID) for one colleague who participates in a coauthorship link. Paired with 'second_colleague_id' to denote a mutual coauthorship between the two colleagues.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or unique ID) for the other colleague in this coauthorship link. Together with 'first_colleague_id' it represents an undirected edge meaning the two have coauthored at least one publication.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct delegates (vertices) in the conference roster. Use this to know how many people are available to consider for seating at the table.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct bilateral agreements (undirected edges) among delegates. Each agreement represents a one-on-one mutual agreement that allows those two delegates to be seated together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first delegate in a reported bilateral agreement pair. Together with delegate_id_2, this denotes two delegates who have a mutual agreement and therefore may sit together.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second delegate in a reported bilateral agreement pair. Paired with delegate_id_1, this is the other endpoint of the undirected edge representing their agreement.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct brands available in the dataset — i.e., how many candidate brands the buyer can choose from for the showcase.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded pairwise collaborations between brands — i.e., how many brand-to-brand links exist showing past teamwork.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a recorded collaboration: the identifier (name or ID) of the first brand in this collaboration pair. Together with brand_b this indicates those two brands have worked together.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a recorded collaboration: the identifier (name or ID) of the second brand in this collaboration pair. Each (brand_a, brand_b) item means the buyer can treat these two as having a mutual collaboration link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct residents being considered as potential board members (the number of vertices in the graph).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct mutual-endorsement relationships among residents — each counts a pair of residents who have formally endorsed each other (the number of undirected edges).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of one resident in a mutually-endorsing pair; together with resident_b this denotes a pair who have formally endorsed one another (one endpoint of an endorsement edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of the other resident in the mutually-endorsing pair; together with resident_a this denotes a pair who have formally endorsed one another (the other endpoint of an endorsement edge).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers represented in the input data — i.e., the number of people (vertices) in the collaboration network at the center. This tells you how many unique volunteers are available to consider when searching for the largest mutually partnered group.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded pairwise partnerships (undirected edges) among volunteers. Each edge counts one distinct past collaboration between two different volunteers; this number measures how many pairwise relationships are documented in the dataset.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a recorded partnership: the unique identifier or name of one volunteer in this documented pair. Because partnerships are undirected, this is simply one member of the pair and the order between u and v does not matter.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the recorded partnership: the unique identifier or name of the second volunteer in this documented pair. Together with volunteer_one_identifier, it denotes a past collaboration between those two distinct volunteers.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct people in the dataset who could be chosen for the interview panel. As the HR lead, treat this as the size of the pool you are selecting from when searching for the largest all-acquainted panel.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of confirmed one-on-one past working relationships between people in the pool. Each such relationship is an undirected link that indicates two people have previously worked together and therefore are compatible to both appear on the same familiar panel.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a confirmed past collaboration: the identifier (e.g., name or ID) for the first person in a pair who have worked together. Used together with person_b_id to represent that these two can co-appear on a panel.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a confirmed past collaboration: the identifier for the second person in a pair. The unordered pair (person_a_id, person_b_id) indicates a mutual past one-on-one working relationship required for any all-acquainted interview panel.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients available for the tasting menu (the number of vertices in the compatibility graph). This tells the solver how many ingredient identifiers exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct compatible ingredient pairs listed (the number of undirected edges). Each pairing indicates two ingredients that complement each other and can coexist in an ensemble.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a compatibility pair: an ingredient identifier (name or index). Together with 'ingredient_b' this entry denotes that these two ingredients pair well.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a compatibility pair: an ingredient identifier (name or index). The pair (ingredient_a, ingredient_b) is unordered and indicates mutual compatibility.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct books being considered for the themed shelf — i.e., the number of vertices in the citation graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of unordered pairs of books that mutually cite or reference one another — i.e., the number of edges in the undirected mutual-citation graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (title, index, or unique ID) for the first book in a mutual-citation pair; one endpoint of an undirected edge meaning this book cites and is cited by the paired book.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second book in the mutual-citation pair; the other endpoint of the edge. Each (u, v) entry denotes two distinct books that reference each other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct cities in the provided travel network — i.e., how many city vertices are available to choose from when building the all-connected itinerary.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unique direct (nonstop) flight connections listed between cities in the network. Each counts an undirected city-to-city route available for the itinerary.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint city identifier for a listed direct flight. Together with the field 'v' this denotes a nonstop connection between two cities (identifiers refer to the city names or IDs used in the input).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint city identifier for a listed direct flight. Paired with 'u', it denotes the nonstop connection between the two cities (undirected — the flight links both ways).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct bands in the dataset — the full pool of acts you can pick from when building the festival roster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded pairwise collaborations between bands (each entry links two different bands who have performed or recorded together). This gives a sense of how many collaboration links exist in the pool.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one band in a collaboration record. Combined with band_b_id, it denotes a pair of bands that have collaborated on stage or in recordings.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other band in a collaboration record. With band_a_id, it forms an undirected collaboration link that must exist between every pair in a valid invited lineup.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of engineers on the roster — i.e., the number of vertices in the review network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct engineer pairs for which there is a mutual review relationship (each engineer in the pair has reviewed the other's code) — i.e., the number of undirected edges.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one engineer in a mutual-review pair. Together with 'v' this denotes a pair of engineers who have reviewed each other's code.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other engineer in the mutual-review pair. Together with 'u' this denotes a pair of engineers who have reviewed each other's code.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct residents being considered for the watch group (the number of vertices in the acquaintance graph). This is the headcount of the candidate pool from which you must select the largest all-acquainted crew.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of mutual, face-to-face acquaintance ties recorded between residents (the number of undirected edges). Each counts one distinct pair of people who personally know each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for one resident at one end of an acquaintance tie. Matches a specific person (by index or name) from the resident list; indicates that this resident personally knows the resident given by 'v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for the other resident at the other end of the acquaintance tie. Together with 'u' it denotes a single mutual, face-to-face connection between two residents (undirected).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct features available to consider for bundling. In the roadmap framing, each graph vertex is a feature; this number tells you how many features exist in the full set from which bundles (=cliques) are formed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of mutual, direct integration links between features across the whole product set. Each undirected edge represents a pair of features that work directly together; this is the overall number of such pairwise compatibilities.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) for one feature in a directly-integrating pair. Paired with 'v', this denotes that feature_id_a and feature_id_b have a direct, mutual integration and can both be included together in a compatible bundle.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) for the other feature in the direct-integration pair. The unordered pair (u, v) indicates a bidirectional compatibility link: both features integrate with each other and are eligible to co-exist in the same fully-compatible bundle.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of students available to invite (the number of vertices in the collaboration graph). Use this to know how many distinct student identifiers appear and to judge clique size against the pool.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of recorded prior pairwise collaborations between students (the number of undirected edges). Each edge represents two students who have previously worked together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one student in a recorded past collaboration (one endpoint of an undirected edge). The order does not matter; this label is used to reference that specific student in the dataset.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other student in the same recorded past collaboration (the other endpoint of the undirected edge). Together with student_a_id it denotes two students who have worked together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct employees considered for forming the committee — i.e., the number of vertices in the company working-relationship graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unique direct working relationships between pairs of employees — i.e., the number of undirected edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a direct working relationship: the identifier (name or ID) of the first employee in a pair that work directly together. Edges are undirected, so this and 'employee_b' denote a mutual link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a direct working relationship: the identifier (name or ID) of the second employee in the pair who works directly with 'employee_a'. Together the pair represents a single mutual working link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct laboratory sensors available to choose from for the bundle; equals the count of vertices in the compatibility graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct compatibility relationships between pairs of sensors; equals the count of undirected edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one sensor in a directly compatible pair. Each entry with this identifier paired with 'sensor_b_id' means these two sensors can work together in the same bundle.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other sensor in a directly compatible pair. Together with 'sensor_a_id' this denotes a direct compatibility link that allows both sensors to coexist in a bundle.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct players listed for the club (the number of vertices in the graph). This counts every player identifier exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded player-pairs who have played together before (the number of undirected edges). Each edge represents a previously played game between that pair.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an undirected edge: the identifier (name or ID) of the first player in a recorded pair who have played together. Order does not matter.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the undirected edge: the identifier (name or ID) of the second player in the recorded pair who have played together. Together with player_id_a this denotes a past game between the two.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct artworks available for selection in the exhibition (i.e., the number of vertices in the graph). Use this to understand the range of artwork identifiers and the maximum possible grouping size.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct thematic links reported between artworks (i.e., the number of undirected edges). Each link indicates a mutual, pairwise thematic relationship that can justify placing two works together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a reported thematic link: the identifier for the first artwork in this pair. Identifiers correspond to distinct artworks (1..total_artworks or given labels) and are used when testing whether a chosen set of works is fully mutually linked.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the reported thematic link: the identifier for the second artwork in this pair. Together with artwork_a_id, this entry means the two named artworks share a direct, mutual thematic connection (undirected).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of software modules available to choose from for the integration plan (i.e., the number of vertices in the graph). Use this to know the size of the module pool when searching for the largest fully interconnected group.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct, pairwise interfaces between modules (i.e., the number of undirected edges). Each edge counts a mutual interface connecting two distinct modules.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of one module that is an endpoint of a direct interface. Order is not significant: this represents one side of a mutual connection between two modules.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of the other module at the other endpoint of the same direct interface. Together with 'module_a' this entry denotes a mutual interface; both must be valid module identifiers from the available pool.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct relatives under consideration (the number of vertices in the compatibility graph). This is how many people could potentially be seated.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise mutual "get-along" relationships among the relatives (the number of undirected edges). Each counted pair represents two relatives who are on good terms and can both be at the same table.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of one relative in a compatible pair. Together with 'v' this denotes that these two relatives get along (an undirected edge between two people).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of the other relative in the compatible pair. The pair (relative_a_id, relative_b_id) indicates a mutual good-terms relationship; order is irrelevant.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of job candidates being considered for the special project — i.e., the number of vertices in the collaboration graph. Each candidate is a distinct person identified by an index or name.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unique past collaborations between candidates — i.e., the number of undirected edges in the graph. Each edge represents a pair of candidates who have previously worked together and therefore can both be on the same invited team.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaboration link: the identifier (index or name) of the first candidate in this collaborating pair. Because collaborations are undirected, this is one member of a two-person past-collaboration tie.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the collaboration link: the identifier (index or name) of the second candidate in this collaborating pair. Together with candidate_a, this denotes a past collaboration that permits both to be selected on the same fully-connected team.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers in the network diagram — the count of vertices (servers) available for selection into the secure cluster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct encrypted links between servers — the count of undirected edges that indicate a secure connection between two servers.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one endpoint server of a specific encrypted link; together with 'v' it names the two servers that share a direct encrypted connection.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other endpoint server of the same encrypted link; paired with 'u' to denote an undirected encrypted connection between the two servers.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct players on the roster (the number of vertices available to choose the starting lineup from).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pairs of roster players who have played together (each counts as an undirected connection between two players).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one player in a pair; together with player_b_id this denotes two roster members who have been on the field together (one endpoint of an undirected teammate relationship).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other player in the pair; paired with player_a_id it denotes that these two distinct roster members have played together (the other endpoint of an undirected teammate relationship).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct academic papers listed in the provided citation dataset. This equals the number of vertices in the citation graph and tells the solver how many paper identifiers exist to consider for forming a mutual-reference roundup.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected edges in the citation graph; each edge corresponds to a pair of papers that mutually cite one another (both papers include a citation to the other). This counts how many mutual-reference relationships are present among the papers.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one paper in a listed mutual-citation pair. Combined with 'paper_b_id', this denotes two papers that each reference the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other paper in the mutual-citation pair. The pair (paper_a_id, paper_b_id) represents a bidirectional citation relationship required for the roundup.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct companies in the partnership network (graph vertices). This is the count of firms available to consider for invitation to the roundtable.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of active pairwise partnerships among the companies (undirected edges). Each partnership listed corresponds to one edge in the graph used to determine which sets of companies form cliques.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an undirected edge: the identifier (ID or label) of the first company in a listed active partnership. Paired with 'v' to indicate these two companies have an active partnership.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an undirected edge: the identifier (ID or label) of the second company in a listed active partnership. Together with 'u', it denotes an active partnership between the two companies.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plant species available in the study pool; each species is a vertex that may be selected for the hybridization set.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected species pairs that are known to hybridize; each counts a pairwise compatibility (an edge) between two species.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one of the two plant species in a compatible pair (one endpoint of an undirected compatibility edge); can be an index or label referring to a specific species in the pool.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other plant species in the compatible pair (the other endpoint of the undirected compatibility edge); together with species_a_id it denotes two species that can hybridize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct garments in the wardrobe pool (each garment corresponds to a vertex). This is the size of the full set you may choose from when assembling the capsule wardrobe.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered compatibility relationships between garments (each is an edge). Each count here represents two specific garments that are considered to 'go with' each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one garment in a compatible pair (one endpoint of an edge). References a specific item from the pool; used together with 'garment_b_id' to indicate those two garments coordinate.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other garment in the compatible pair (the other endpoint of the edge). Together with 'garment_a_id' it denotes an undirected compatibility link between two distinct garments.
